From the Community Manager

Your Feedback Matters

Feedback is an important part of helping us understand what is working well within our community, as well as where we can continue to improve.

All feedback received is entered into our feedback system and reviewed by me. Where appropriate, I will also follow up directly with the resident who provided the feedback so we can discuss their concerns, suggestions, or ideas further.

If you would like to provide feedback at any time, you can find our feedback box on the table under the TV, opposite Reception. You are also always welcome to come and have a chat with me directly.

Thank You for Your Bus Feedback

Thank you to everyone who took the time to complete our recent bus survey. We received some great feedback and suggestions, which have given us valuable insight into what residents would like from our bus service.

We have taken all your feedback on board and are currently looking into the ideas and options raised. Thank you for having your say and helping us consider how the service can best support our community.

Melody Ridge Centre Refurbishment

As many of you may be aware, plans are underway for the upcoming refurbishment of the Melody Ridge Centre. While we don't yet have confirmed dates to share, I wanted to give everyone an early heads-up about what this will mean for our community while the works are taking place.

During the refurbishment, activities normally held at Melody Ridge will temporarily relocate to the Manor. This will mean a little more activity than usual and, importantly, some sharing of spaces across our community.

When the time comes, I ask everyone to bring a little patience, kindness, and flexibility as we adjust to these temporary arrangements together. There may be times when spaces or usual routines need to change, and we will do our best to keep everyone informed and minimise disruption along the way.

Further information, including dates and arrangements, will be shared as soon as these details are confirmed.

Food Focus meetings are back

Our food focus meetings are returning! These meetings are a great opportunity for residents to share their thoughts, suggestions, and feedback about our dining experience with the team. Whether you have ideas for the menu, comments about the meals or simply want to be a part of the conversation, we encourage you to come along. Our next food focus meeting will be held on Thursday 13th August at 12:45pm in the dining room. We look forward to seeing you there and hearing your ideas and feedback.

As always, thank you for your continued feedback, understanding, and contribution to our community.

Warm regards,
Candice

Poetry Club

The Poetry Club meets on the second Sunday of the month at the Manor at 2pm. Next month Haiku is the challenge. Haiku is a traditional Japanese poetic form consisting of three untuned lines with a 5,7 and 5 syllable structure.

Weeds

I was pottering in the garden
just looking to and fro
When suddenly I began to think
Why weeds? I want to know!

It doesn't matter what I do
the weeds just keep appearing
I mulch and regularly check
but there's always more...I'm tearing my hair!

I mean, what is the point, I say
What purpose do they fill?
Flowers bring beauty, trees give shade
But weeds? Their value's surely nil!

Except to frustrate gardeners
with backaches or sunburn
and effort time and time again
full knowing they'll return.

And there'll be more, so what to do?
but accept the good and bad,
And thank the Lord that I can still
bend down and... pull the blighters out!!
— Judy B.

Shopping Bus

From the Sales Team

Dear Residents,

With the end of winter upon us, there's a sense of change in the air. For many of us it's that time of year when we start thinking about spring cleaning and decluttering. The inevitable accumulation of life's belongings can have us questioning all the items that could find a better home.

If you are finding it isolated living in the Villas maybe it's time to have a look at the Apartments in The Manor where you are close to the activities, the restaurant, nurse, where it can be a more manageable home in a central community location might start to look very appealing. This is where Aveo can make a significant difference, with our Move with Ease program. Designed to simplify the transition to a new home, we make it as smooth and stress-free as possible.

Does this sound like something you or a neighbour might be interested in? Reach out to us to learn more about the possibilities that can lead you to a life of comfort, convenience, and greater financial freedom.

We have no stock for sale and one settlement coming soon.

Regards,
Debbie & Maree — Sales

Sales Open House — Day 5th August

Social Club News

The inaugural Social Club Resident Speaker presentation and morning tea kicked off with Pam Cranny sharing her story of "Going to Nigeria". Forty residents attended the entertaining and informative insight into a part of the world that most of us will never experience. Thanks to Pam for all the effort she put into sharing her and Peter's experiences. Don't forget to contact a member of the Social Club Committee if you have a life story you would like to share with residents in a similar manner.

August is EKKA month! If you're missing those strawberry sundae ice creams, come to Fountain Court from 11.30am on Exhibition Wednesday (12 August) for a sausage sizzle and strawberry sundae ice cream. For catering purposes, register by Friday 7 August on sheets in the Manor, MRC or online on the Residents' Hub. Payment of $5 collected on the day. BYO drinks.

The musical screening for this month on Sunday 16 August in the Melody Ridge Centre (MRC) will be "Rigoletto", an opera in three acts by Giuseppe Verdi. A Metropolitan production, it stars Placido Domingo in the leading role of the Duke of Mantova. Cost $3. RSVP on the sheets in the Manor or MRC.

The Social Club is trialling opening the bar every Friday from 3.30pm to 5.30pm, with nibbles supplied on the first Friday of the month. Non-alcoholic and alcoholic beverages are available. On Friday 21 August the popular musician and singer, Rob Rosenlund, will be performing at the Happy Hour in the MRC. Come along to this free event (BYO nibbles) which will be the last Social Club event in the MRC before the refurbishment. There will be no Social Club Happy Hour on 28 August but the Bar will be in operation in The Manor from Friday 4 September.

Date Claimer: A Fashion Parade by online retailer Tulio Fashion will be held in The Manor on Wednesday 2 September, accompanied by Morning Tea. Cash and credit cards accepted for orders on the day. RSVP by Friday 28 August on sheets in the Manor, MRC or online on the Residents' Hub. Seating from 9.30am for a 10am start. Cost: $10. Payment may be made during Happy Hours, or on Tuesday 25 August in The Manor (10am to 10.30am) or on the day.

Future events: A busy calendar of events has been planned by the Social Club Committee for the coming months including Fortunato Isgro (who performed at the Soup and Pizza night) booked for a Dance Party (Saturday 3 October) and our Christmas lunch (2 December). With the refurbishment of the MRC, we ask your patience as we run events at The Manor and may need some 'work arounds'. As always, if you have any questions or comments, please feel free to contact me.

Kathy Kingsford (Convenor)
bdsc.convenor@gmail.com
Mob: 0428 699 455

The Sergeant and His Mate

We wandered into Pambula
One Tuesday late,
And who should come along,
But the Sergeant and his mate.
He said "High Neville, you have nothing to fear"
But we have three warrants for you
So you had better come up here
He looked at me and asked my name
I replied it was Ron.
They looked and replied "Come along".

We were taken to the Station
And they put Neville down the back
They started to ask me more questions
About this and that
But there were none I could answer
And my mind was far away
Till they found a quart of paint
On the back seat of my car
And after they had booked me
They put me in a cell.

The Constable went to Eden
To see what Mournful could tell
He found him at Woodies
On the outskirts of the town
Come fix your old Ford
For it had broken down
He took him to Pambula
To the car they went to see
The first thing they looked at
Was the battery.

That Battery is stolen
And there is other stuff as well
But Mournful denied it
So they put him in a cell
Four days they did question him
Till at last he did give in
He said "I'll take you to the stuff"
If they would leave the blame on him
Out to the stuff they did go
But it was not all there.

So off they went to Eden
And brought back another pair
Doug and Harley is their names
One night in the cells they did stay
One hundred pounds bail and their pains
And they knew people who would pay
Now in the jail house
To Neville, Mournful and Ron
The time they will spend there
God only knows how long.

Now you had better behave around Pambula
And we are warning you mate
That if you don't you will end up
Behind that iron gate
For Sergeant Bowers and Constable Rowney
Are the long arm of the law
And brother if you don't behave
You will be behind that gate some more.
